brief: UBS's morning note frames the AI trade as the main drag on Friday's close (S&P 500 -1.8%, Nasdaq -2.9%), driven by sharp declines in semis, memory and neocloud names including NVDA (-4.2%). Monday brings a partial bounce (EStoxx +20bps, futures +40/+80bps) while a bid to Treasuries, yields down 2-8bps with the curve steepening, raises growth-scare concern. Asia is mixed: Tokyo Electron (+6.5%) eases the semi-cap complex after earnings, but Kioxia's 16% drop on a softer outlook keeps the guidance bar high; UBS says the AI complex needs more than one positive Tokyo print to signal the derisking is over. Crude is down 3-3.5% on reports Trump will give Iran diplomacy more time before Tuesday's midterms, which UBS frames as the pivot for both the Iran timeline and risk appetite. Week ahead: midterms Tuesday, BoE expected to hike 25bp to 4% Thursday, US payrolls (65k expected vs 29k prior) Friday. Friday's European cash flow finished balanced (48/52), 20% below the YTD average, with Banks busiest (demand in Spain/Netherlands, supply in Italy) and Technology and Telecoms for sale.
